title: A spectral gap for Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm with a uniformly randomized step size
summary: Let $π(\mathrm{d} x)\propto e^{-U(x)}\, \mathrm{d} x$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $U$ is continuously differentiable and $m$-strongly convex with a globally $L$-Lipschitz gradient, $0 1$, for all square-integrable functions, the ratio of the Monte Carlo asymptotic variance relative to independence sampling has an upper bound of order $\sqrt{d \log d}$. This contrasts with fixed-MALA, where the ratio can be as bad as $d/\log d$ in thew worst-case scenario. The spectral gap also gives geometric convergence of the lazy kernel from every initial density in $L^2(π)$, central limit theorems, and…
